relations.subject: Keiji Nishitani
relations.evidence: He was a scholar of the Kyoto School and a disciple of Kitarō Nishida.

relations.subject: Keiji Nishitani
relations.evidence: In 1924, Nishitani received his doctorate from Kyoto Imperial University for his dissertation "Das Ideale und das Reale bei Schelling und Bergson".

relations.subject: Keiji Nishitani
relations.evidence: He studied under Martin Heidegger in Freiburg from 1937 to 1939.

relations.subject: Keiji Nishitani
relations.evidence: he enrolled into the philosophy department of the Kyoto Imperial University, where he studied under Nishida Kitarō and Tanabe Hajime

relations.subject: Keiji Nishitani
relations.evidence: After his graduation in 1924 he taught philosophy at local highschools for eight years and assumed a lectureship in the Ôtani University until 1935.

relations.subject: Keiji Nishitani
relations.evidence: appointed to go to the University of Freiburg, where he spent two years studying under Heidegger.

relations.subject: Keiji Nishitani
relations.role: principal Chair of Philosophy and Religion
relations.evidence: Nishitani held the principal Chair of Philosophy and Religion at Kyoto University from 1943 until becoming emeritus in 1964.

relations.subject: Keiji Nishitani
relations.evidence: He then taught philosophy and religion at Ōtani University.
